[[File:Miho-jinja_haiden.jpg|thumb|250px|{{ill|Miho Shrine|en|Miho Shrine|qid=Q3313076|lt=Miho Shrine}}]]

'''Ebisu Shrines''' (えびす神社) are {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrines}} dedicated to {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|en|Ebisu (mythology)|qid=Q1129330|lt=Ebisu}}, {{ill|Hiruko|ja|ヒルコ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiruko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067028}}, or {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|en|Kotoshironushi|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi}}.
== Overview ==
Ebisu shrines are found throughout Japan and may be written as '''夷神社''', '''戎神社''', '''胡神社''', '''蛭子神社''', '''恵比須神社''', '''恵比寿神社''', '''恵美須神社''', or '''恵毘須神社'''. Even shrines whose official names do not contain "Ebisu" may be commonly referred to as "○○ Ebisu Shrine" if they enshrine Ebisu. In the {{ill|Kansai|ja|関西|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kansai region|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1111292}}, Ebisu is often affectionately called ''Ebbesan'' or ''Obessan.''
Some shrines named "Hiruko Shrine" (蛭子神社) are pronounced "Hiruko Jinja" instead of "Ebisu Jinja" because they specifically enshrine {{ill|Hiruko|ja|蛭子神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiruko-no-Kami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1067028|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067028}}. However, due to the syncretism and identification of Hiruko with Ebisu, some shrines enshrine Hiruko but are still called "Ebisu Shrine." Conversely, there are shrines named "Hiruko Shrine" that enshrine Kotoshironushi instead of Hiruko.
